## What each solver holds fixed (`ThermoX`, `ThermoY`, `extrapolate_dlnp`, `Kinetics`) {#sec-ch01b-state}

### Summary

A parcel of fixed elemental make-up has its state fixed by two thermodynamic variables once its reactions are in
equilibrium. Each kintera solver chooses a different pair to hold fixed and returns the rest: temperature and
pressure, or internal energy and volume, or entropy along a pressure step. This section states the pair for every
entry point and the conservation laws its step obeys. It also gives the one consequence a model builder must not
miss: a dynamical core that conserves energy and volume has to call the energy-and-volume path.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** One table of entry point, fixed variables and conserved quantities, @tbl-ch01b-state-table.

**Data.** Molar amounts of gases and condensates (passed as concentrations, mass fractions or mole fractions); two
state variables.

**Placement.** Read before chapters 3 to 6; a map of their solvers.

**Activation.** Not applicable: it describes the solvers; it has no option of its own.

**Guarantee / limits.** Element amounts (and element/dry ratios) exact for balanced reactions; element-weighted
mole fractions are not conserved; energy, entropy to the solver tolerance.

**Evidence.** The conservation lines of the chapter 3, 4 and 6 checks; see the Tests layer.
:::

Local symbols: $N_i$, molar amount of species $i$ in the parcel [mol]; $x_i = N_i/\sum_j N_j$, its mole fraction
(a normalized quantity, not an amount); $c_i = N_i/V$, its concentration in a parcel of volume $V$
[$\mathrm{mol\,m^{-3}}$]; $S$, the stoichiometric matrix with entries $S_{ir}$; $\xi_r$, extent of reaction $r$
[mol]; $a_{ei}$, number of atoms of element $e$ in species $i$; $u_i(T)$, molar internal energy of species $i$
[$\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}}$]; $U_{\mathrm{p}} = \sum_i N_i u_i$, internal energy of the parcel [J]; $U = U_{\mathrm{p}}/V$, internal
energy per volume [$\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$]; $C_V = \sum_i c_i\, c_{v,i}$, heat capacity at constant volume per volume
[$\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}\,K^{-1}}$].

### Derivation

**Step 1: counting.** A parcel has one molar amount per species and two thermodynamic variables. The solvers do not
move amounts freely. They move them along reactions, so every reachable composition is

$$
N = N^0 + S \xi ,
$$ {#eq-ch01b-state-extent}

with $N^0$ the starting amounts and one extent $\xi_r$ per reaction. The relation holds for molar amounts, and for
concentrations only at fixed volume ($c = c^0 + S\xi/V$). It does not hold for mole fractions when a reaction
changes the number of moles ($\sum_i S_{ir} \ne 0$, for example $\mathrm{NH_3 + H_2S \to NH_4SH(s)}$). Each active reaction at equilibrium adds one
condition: its reaction Gibbs energy is zero, or, for a phase change, its saturation condition holds
(@sec-ch04-conditions). With $R$ active reactions there are $R$ unknown extents and $R$ conditions, so once the
starting amounts and the two thermodynamic variables are given, the system is square and determines the state.
This counting holds as written when $T$ is one of the two given variables. When $U$ and $V$ are given instead, $T$ is
one more unknown and the energy balance $\sum_i c_i u_i(T) = U$ one more condition, so there are $R + 1$ unknowns
and $R + 1$ conditions and the system is again square (@sec-ch04-equilibrate-uv).
Inactive reactions, such as a condensate that is absent and stays absent, are inequalities, not conditions; that is
why the phase solvers are active-set methods (@sec-ch04-active-set). `equilibrate_tp` ({{< code src/thermo/equilibrate_tp.h >}})
works in mole fractions. Each iteration subtracts the active stoichiometric columns times the step from $x$, which
is @eq-ch01b-state-extent for a parcel of one mole at the start of the step, and then divides by the new sum
$\sum_i x_i$. That rescales every amount by the same factor and changes no ratio of amounts. So the returned $x$ is
$N/\sum_j N_j$ for amounts $N$ that obey @eq-ch01b-state-extent; the dry species, which is in no reaction, keeps
its amount, so $N_i = x_i\, N_{\mathrm{dry}}/x_{\mathrm{dry}}$ recovers them. `phase_equilibrate_tp`
({{< code src/equilibrium/phase_equilibrate_tp.h >}}) applies @eq-ch01b-state-extent to its amounts directly.

**Step 2: elements are conserved by every step.** A reaction is balanced when it has as many atoms of each element
on both sides, $\sum_i a_{ei} S_{ir} = 0$ for every element $e$ and reaction $r$. Applying the element matrix to
@eq-ch01b-state-extent,

$$
\sum_i a_{ei}\, N_i = \sum_i a_{ei}\, N_i^0 + \sum_r \Big(\sum_i a_{ei} S_{ir}\Big) \xi_r = \sum_i a_{ei}\, N_i^0 ,
$$ {#eq-ch01b-state-elements}

for any extents, so element amounts are conserved exactly by every solver that moves along reactions, the kinetics
included (@sec-ch06-mass-action). The conserved budgets are amounts, or ratios of amounts. The element-weighted mole
fraction $\sum_i a_{ei} x_i = \sum_i a_{ei} N_i / \sum_j N_j$ is not conserved when the number of moles changes.
For $\mathrm{A + B \to C}$ from $x = (0.4, 0.3, 0.3)$ with $\xi = 0.1$ mol per mole, the A atoms stay at 0.7 mol,
while their mole-fraction weight goes from 0.7 to $0.7/0.9 = 0.778$. A host that compares budgets per mole uses
element/dry ratios $\sum_i a_{ei} N_i / N_{\mathrm{dry}}$ (or element/mass), which are ratios of amounts and are
conserved. The chemical-equilibrium reader rejects a reaction that does not conserve every
element to $10^{-10}$ (`EquilibriumOptionsImpl::from_yaml`,
{{< code src/equilibrium/equilibrium_options.cpp EquilibriumOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}), so for the log-K solver the
balance is enforced on input. The thermodynamics (nucleation) and kinetics readers do not check it (searched in
`src`), so for those cards @eq-ch01b-state-elements holds only if the input is balanced.

**Step 3: the two fixed variables of each solver.**

- *Temperature and pressure.* `ThermoX.forward` ({{< code src/thermo/thermo_x.cpp ThermoXImpl::forward >}}) takes $T$,
  $p$ and mole fractions, overwrites the mole fractions in place with the equilibrium ones, and returns the gain
  matrix (@sec-ch04-equilibrate-tp). At fixed $T$ and $p$ the equilibrium is the minimum
  of the Gibbs energy subject to @eq-ch01b-state-elements (@sec-ch04-conditions). The amounts change, $T$ and $p$ do
  not. The parcel's volume changes with its gas amount, $\Delta V = (\mathcal R T/p) \sum_g \Delta N_g$ for an
  ideal gas with the condensate volume neglected, and its internal energy $U_{\mathrm{p}}$ is not conserved.
- *Internal energy and volume.* `ThermoY.forward` ({{< code src/thermo/thermo_y.cpp ThermoYImpl::forward >}}) takes
  density, internal energy per volume and mass fractions, overwrites the mass fractions in place and returns the gain
  matrix. The volume is fixed by the density, and $U$ is held. Inside the kernel, after every change of the amounts,
  `equilibrate_uv` ({{< code src/thermo/equilibrate_uv.h equilibrate_uv >}}) solves $\sum_i c_i u_i(T) = U$ for $T$
  by Newton's method,

$$
T \leftarrow T + \frac{U - \sum_i c_i\, u_i(T)}{\sum_i c_i\, \mathrm{d}u_i/\mathrm{d}T} ,
$$ {#eq-ch01b-state-t-of-u}

  whose denominator is $C_V$ (@sec-ch04-equilibrate-uv), with the kernel's energy model (linear with offsets, plus the per-species extra
  function; @sec-ch01b-shared, Step 4). That temperature is
  a temporary of the kernel and is not returned. A host gets $T$ by calling `compute("VU->T")` afterwards, which runs
  the same Newton step with `eval_intEng_R` and `eval_cv_R`
  ({{< code src/thermo/thermo_y.cpp ThermoYImpl::_intEng_to_temp >}}).
- *Entropy along a pressure step.* `extrapolate_dlnp`
  ({{< code src/thermo/extrapolate_ad.cpp ThermoXImpl::extrapolate_dlnp >}}) moves the parcel to $p\, e^{\Delta \ln p}$
  and finds the temperature at which the molar entropy equals its starting value (plus an optional prescribed
  change). With rain-out the target is the entropy left in the gas after the condensate leaves with its own entropy
  (@sec-ch03-adiabat).
- *Internal energy and volume, in time.* With `evolve_temperature`, the kinetics Jacobian
  ({{< code src/kinetics/kinetics.cpp KineticsImpl::jacobian >}}) differentiates the rates at fixed $U$ and volume,
  $(\partial T/\partial c_k)_U = -u_k/C_V$ (@sec-ch06-jacobian). Without it the rates are differentiated at fixed
  $T$.
- *Temperature, pressure and elements, for chemical equilibrium.* The log-K solver of @sec-ch05 holds $T$, $p$ and
  the element totals, with every amount kept above a floor ({{< code src/equilibrium/phase_equilibrate_tp.h >}}).

| entry point | holds fixed | returns | conserves exactly |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ThermoX.forward` | $T$, $p$ | gain matrix; mole fractions updated in place | element amounts (element/dry ratios of $x$; not element-weighted fractions) |
| `ThermoY.forward` | $U$, $V$ | gain matrix; mass fractions updated in place; $T$ from `compute("VU->T")` | elements; $U$ to the $T$ tolerance |
| `extrapolate_dlnp` | molar $s$ on the new $p$ | nothing; $T$ and mole fractions updated in place | elements (reversible step) |
| `Kinetics` with `evolve_temperature` | $U$, $V$ (linearised) | rates, Jacobian | elements |
| log-K solver (@sec-ch05) | $T$, $p$ | equilibrium amounts | elements (balance checked on input) |

: The variables each solver holds fixed. {#tbl-ch01b-state-table}

**Step 4: consequence for coupling.** A finite-volume dynamical core advances the conserved densities, mass and
total energy, in a cell of fixed volume. What it hands to the thermodynamics is therefore $\rho$, $U$ and the mass
fractions, and the adjustment it needs is the one at fixed $U$ and $V$. Calling the temperature-and-pressure path
with the core's $T$ and $p$ instead holds $T$ fixed while vapour condenses. In molar amounts, the parcel's internal
energy then changes by

$$
\Delta U_{\mathrm{p}} = \sum_i u_i(T)\, \Delta N_i = \sum_r \Big(\sum_i S_{ir}\, u_i(T)\Big) \xi_r = -\sum_r L_r\, \xi_r
\quad [\mathrm{J}] ,
$$ {#eq-ch01b-state-energy-change}

for the fixed-$T$ path of `ThermoX.forward` ({{< code src/thermo/thermo_x.cpp ThermoXImpl::forward >}}), with
$L_r = -\sum_i S_{ir} u_i$ the latent energy of reaction $r$ (positive for condensation) and $\Delta N = S\xi$ from
@eq-ch01b-state-extent. This is not zero unless no latent energy is released. At fixed $p$ the parcel also changes
volume by $\Delta V$ (above), so the TP path gives no energy per volume of its own. A host of fixed volume $V$
converts explicitly: it passes $x_i = c_i / \sum_j c_j$, and maps the returned fractions back to concentrations at
its own $V$ with its dry amount kept, $c_i' = c_{\mathrm{dry}}\, x_i'/x_{\mathrm{dry}}'$. In that fixed-volume basis
$\Delta c = S\xi/V$, the energy per volume changes by $\Delta U = -\sum_r L_r \xi_r / V$, and the pressure is no
longer the $p$ the solver held, because the gas amount changed. Either way the fixed-$T$ path does not conserve
energy, and the energy-conserving coupling uses `ThermoY.forward` (@sec-ch14-saturation).

No published derivation is quoted. The steps above are standard equilibrium thermodynamics, here matched to the code
at the pin.

### Numerical method

No numerical method of its own: each solver's iteration is described in its chapter (@sec-ch04-equilibrate-tp,
@sec-ch04-equilibrate-uv, @sec-ch03-adiabat, @sec-ch06-jacobian, @sec-ch05-newton). The figure of the parcel and its
solvers is not provided: the figure module is not written yet.

### Code

| what | code link | symbol | switch |
|---|---|---|---|
| fixed $T$, $p$ | {{< code src/thermo/thermo_x.cpp ThermoXImpl::forward >}} | `ThermoXImpl::forward` | always |
| fixed $U$, $V$ | {{< code src/thermo/thermo_y.cpp ThermoYImpl::forward >}} | `ThermoYImpl::forward` | always |
| $T$ from $U$ | {{< code src/thermo/equilibrate_uv.h equilibrate_uv >}} | `equilibrate_uv` | `uv-solver` |
| entropy step | {{< code src/thermo/extrapolate_ad.cpp ThermoXImpl::extrapolate_dlnp >}} | `extrapolate_dlnp` | `rainout` |
| fixed-$U$ Jacobian | {{< code src/kinetics/kinetics.cpp KineticsImpl::jacobian >}} | `KineticsImpl::jacobian` | `evolve_temperature` |

: Checks of the fixed variables. {#tbl-ch01b-state-tests}

The checks are collected here, not repeated. At fixed $T$ and $p$ the element/dry ratios change by at most
$5.6 \times 10^{-16}$ (relative; round-off).[^ch01b-tp] The amounts check reproduces the $\mathrm{A + B \to C}$
example above (amount change $1.1 \times 10^{-16}$, fraction weight change 0.078) and runs `ThermoX.forward` on
`tests/jupiter.yaml` at 160, 200 and 250 K. The amounts recovered per mole of dry gas differ from the start by
$S\xi$ to $3.7 \times 10^{-16}$ (relative), and the element/dry ratios are kept to $5.2 \times 10^{-16}$. The
element-weighted mole fractions change by about $8.0 \times 10^{-5}$ where $\mathrm{NH_4SH(s)}$ forms, and the gas
volume by up to 0.27 % (informational lines).[^ch01b-am] It also prints $\sum_i u_i \Delta N_i$ next to
$-\sum_r L_r \xi_r$ with the deck's linear energies; that is an identity once $\Delta N = S\xi$, not a test of
the code, so @eq-ch01b-state-energy-change has no check of its own.

### Limits

- Element conservation needs balanced reactions. Only the chemical-equilibrium reader checks the balance; the
  thermodynamics and kinetics readers do not.
- The fixed-$U$ statements hold to the tolerance of the temperature inversion and of the solver, not exactly;
  at the pin `check_ch4_uv.py` records an expected failure of the partition method near 300 K (an open defect of
  @sec-ch04-equilibrate-uv).
- The kinetics holds $U$ only in its linearisation. A step of @sec-ch06-implicit is not followed by a temperature
  update from $U$ inside kintera; the caller does that.
